note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of known prostate adenocarcinoma following recent PSA rise and repeat biopsy.

The patient is a 63-year-old retired carpenter with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed on biopsy in June 2024. He resides independently in a retirement community and is married, with his wife as his primary contact. He has a medical history of TURT and is currently not on any active medication. His PSA has risen from 7.7 ng/mL in December 2023 to 12.0 ng/mL in February 2025. He plays tennis twice weekly and consumes approximately one unit of alcohol per week. Recent appointments include a stable cardiology review in autumn 2024 and routine dental and radiology checks. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 16/35. He travels over 60 minutes by train to the clinic for appointments.

On digital rectal examination, a suspicious nodule is palpated in the prostate, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, including a blood pressure of 145/81 mmHg and heart rate of 70 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses are noted.
